evidence_edges.note: P0D identifies herself as a pixie; no inference about all pixie life, captivity or fate.
Blood Skunk names his own people while disputing affiliation with the clowns; not proof of Council of Clowns membership.
Stanley's father is Delit Or'Nath; the father-name orthography is owner-confirmed and the played episode refers to the family, without proving burial, rescue or other parentage.
Stanley physically hands the mask to Hope, who forms and wears it as a crown; no new attunement, permanent legal ownership or subsequent custody is inferred.

entities.description: Intelligent lizardfolk peoples, including Golden Land hunters and the distinct Razak Val clans. Their local Great Fang traditions are not universal traits; after Earth's restoration Vorel leads a surviving group toward Razak Val, without a witnessed reconstruction.
questions: Groxl's origin narrative and local creation stories are testimony, not independently verified general ancestry.
The group's arrival at and rebuilding of Razak Val are not shown.

entities.description: Tiefling peoples connected with T'ietkalla and its displaced communities. Nobieri's ancient royal account is attributed testimony; Hope's coronation and the Harbor's founding are witnessed, while T'ietkalla's reconstruction remains incomplete.
questions: Ancient Akmenos genealogy and supernatural pacts are not independently established as species-wide history.
T'ietkalla's final rebuilding and a complete survivor census are not witnessed.

entities.description: Dwarves are encountered as Oilbeard guards at the Black Mine and as residents of Burp; these distinct communities do not establish one common dwarven government or set of customs.
questions: The Oilbeards' mine-ownership, uprising and population figures are interested testimony, not a dwarven-wide political history.
Burp's older founder, economy and the wider dwarven population are not independently established.

entities.description: The Elhandari receive travelers in a large inhabited forest station; their elder's accounts of ancient planetary work and spiritual law belong to that community, not to all elves.
questions: Elhandari ancient history and beliefs are attributed accounts; the group is not interchangeable with every elven community.
The High Elf's attempted memory sharing is declined, not a completed memory transfer.

entities.description: Blood Skunk identifies as Harlequinari and is treated as an outsider by the Council of Clowns; the council's connections do not establish that all its members are Harlequinari.
questions: Neither a complete Council of Clowns membership census nor universal Harlequinari appearance, abilities or rules of exile are established.
Blood Skunk's estrangement is documented, but the circumstances of his earlier departure are not.

entities.description: Illithids are encountered through a headset-mediated CHIDS office and through a contestant at Sigil's M-fighting championship; neither context establishes a single motive or culture for every illithid.
questions: Charles Dickens's explanation of the Void Realm and its invasion plans is interested testimony, not a verified universal illithid program.
Fax/Faks spelling and subsequent absence are unresolved; the CHIDS living-wall council must not be merged with illithids.

entities.description: An armed orc enforces the Principal's authority on the road to Slavetown, while an unrelated orc is encountered in the Gray Waste; neither role represents all orcs or their political allegiance.
questions: Koromukishi/Kuromokishi order membership is not a universal orc ancestry or culture; its spelling remains source-provisional.
The Gray Waste orc's continued responsiveness after decapitation is an exceptional scene, not an established biological rule.

entities.description: P0D is a pixie who reports forced captivity and Pixie Blush production; other transformed pixies are seen reverting near T'ietkalla, without proving a general pixie origin or universal transformation rule.
questions: P0D's account of Farmer Dewey's wider operation is testimony; the farm is not fully inspected in E031.
The cause of later pixie-hulk reversions and fate of all captives remain unverified; the alternate Pod is not P0D revived.

entities.description: A pixie companion encountered in Trashburg who identifies herself by an aquarium label containing the numeral zero; her account of the wider farm's production is testimony, not a witnessed inventory.
questions: The alternate Pod at Tower Nash is a distinct counterpart, not this individual returned to life.
P0D is killed in E050; her subsequent E056 spirit appearance is not bodily survival.

entities.description: A member of Hope's separate traveling party who identifies himself as Harlequinari while explicitly rejecting affiliation with the Council of Clowns.
questions: He reports having left Harlequinari society; no full formal-exile history or council membership is established.
His later S3E01 death must not be confused with S3E02 reuse of his inert head.

entities.description: Stanley Billings's father, whose owner-confirmed written name is Delit Or'Nath; E115 recounts the father's scientific interests and Stanley's understanding of his death.
questions: Name is confirmed from owner/player-written evidence, not a direct original-audio spelling check.
E115 does not establish an actual recovery, resurrection, or the definitive site of his remains; any later status requires separate source review.

entities.description: The magical mask connected with Stanley's Fate Six; Stanley physically transfers it to Hope in S3E18, and Hope wears it as a crown without demonstrated completed attunement.
questions: Receipt and wearing are witnessed; Hope's new attunement and independent command of the ship are not demonstrated in the handover.
This event alone does not establish perpetual future custody, ship ownership or the restoration of every ghost sailor.
